notes.title: 3B staffing — March
notes.content:
Establishment is eight nurses on days. We have run at six or seven for most of March.

That is why the second pilot training round did not happen here — Patrick offered it and I said no, twice. Four hours of a nurse's time when we are two down is four hours the floor does not have.

The shortfall is not a fact I put in writing anywhere a vendor could read.

notes.title: Pilot — the nursing view
notes.content:
The doctors like it more than we do. The documentation it saves is theirs; the interruptions it creates land on us, because when a workstation drops a session mid-note the clinician turns round and asks the nearest nurse.

That is not a complaint about the product. It is a fact about where the cost lands and nobody has asked us.

notes.title: Roster — why it does not leave the unit
notes.content:
Two reasons. It is staff personal information. And a roster read across two weeks tells you exactly which nights this unit is thinnest, which is not something I hand out.

Managers get coverage confirmed. They do not get the grid.

notes.title: Swap protocol
notes.content: Two nurses agree, both tell me, I check the resulting shift against safe staffing, I approve or I do not. No swap that leaves a shift below establishment gets approved regardless of who is asking or why.

notes.title: Census — Q1
notes.content: Averaged 26 of 28 beds. Two short-stay surges in February. No capacity impact from the pilot, which is worth recording because that was the fear.

notes.title: Unit 3B — establishment and reality
notes.content:
Twenty-eight beds. Establishment eight registered nurses on days, six on nights, plus support staff.

We have run below establishment most of this year. Below establishment is a staffing number; what it means on the floor is that nobody gets a break.

notes.title: Skill mix
notes.content:
Three nurses with more than ten years, four in their first three, one newly qualified.

That shape works if the experienced ones are spread across shifts and falls apart if two are off together, which the roster tries to prevent and cannot always.

notes.title: Handover — nursing
notes.content:
Bedside handover, twenty minutes, structured.

Doing it at the bedside rather than in the office was contentious for about six months and now nobody would go back.

notes.title: Falls and pressure areas
notes.content:
Two falls this quarter, neither with harm. Pressure area incidence below target.

These are the numbers a ward is judged on and they correlate with staffing more than with any intervention, which is not what anyone wants to hear.

notes.title: Preceptorship
notes.content:
The newly qualified nurse has a named preceptor and protected supernumerary time.

Protected until the ward is short, at which point it is the first thing that goes, which defeats the point of protecting it.

notes.title: Break coverage
notes.content:
The thing that silently fails first. Nobody records a missed break and everybody has them.

If I recorded them honestly the numbers would be a scandal, and the reason I do not is that I have nothing to offer the people who would be in them.

notes.title: Discharge coordination
notes.content:
Nursing does most of the practical discharge work and none of the discharge decision.

That split is normal and it is why discharge lounges get used late and reluctantly.

notes.title: Agency and bank staff
notes.content:
Bank first, agency second. Bank staff know the ward; agency staff need orientation, which costs the substantive team time on an already short shift.

An agency shift is not equivalent to a substantive one and the finance report treats them as identical.

notes.title: Mandatory training compliance
notes.content:
89% against a 95% target. The gap is entirely people who have been too busy on shift to do e-learning.

The solution offered is to do it at home, which is unpaid work, which is why it does not happen.

notes.title: Ward rounds — timing
notes.content:
Consultant rounds start between 08:30 and 11:00 depending on who is on. Nursing plans the day around a round whose time is unpredictable.

Raised for years. Never resolved.

notes.title: What a charge nurse actually does
notes.content:
Allocate, escalate, protect. Allocate the workload, escalate what the team cannot solve, protect the team from everything that is not patient care.

Most of the job is the third one and none of it appears in the job description.

notes.title: Falls and pressure ulcers
notes.content: Two falls this month, no harm. Pressure ulcer incidence at target. Both metrics move with staffing and everyone knows it and the reports never say it.

notes.title: Bank and agency on the unit
notes.content: Roughly one shift in five is covered by bank or agency. An agency nurse who does not know the unit is safer than no nurse and slower than a regular, and the sums never capture the second part.

notes.title: Escalation — when I call the site manager
notes.content: Below safe staffing, an unmanageable acuity mix, or a bed I cannot safely fill. Three reasons and I have used all three this month.

notes.title: Student nurses
notes.content: Two on placement. Mentoring is unfunded time and it happens because people do it, not because it is rostered.

notes.title: Why the roster does not leave the unit
notes.content: It is staff personal information, and read across two weeks it tells anyone exactly which nights we are thinnest. Managers get coverage confirmed; nobody gets the grid.

notes.title: Swap requests
notes.content: Three or four a fortnight. I approve the ones that leave the shift safe and decline the ones that do not, and the second kind is always urgent and always someone I like.

notes.title: What the documentation pilot costs nursing
notes.content: When a workstation drops a doctor's session mid-note, the doctor turns round and asks the nearest nurse. Nobody counted that and nobody asked us.

todos.title: Hold the line on the second training round
todos.content: Asked twice. The hours do not exist while we are two down.

todos.title: Get the nursing-side cost of the timeout in front of Kenji
todos.content: Nobody has asked us and it lands on us.

todos.content: First thing that goes, which defeats the point.

todos.content: 'Do it at home' is unpaid work.

todos.content: Nothing to offer the people it would name.
